data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fetch budget must be denominated in both requests and bytes, and exhaustion must be recorded as a typed terminal event that includes a cryptographic hash of the budget policy and the cumulative counters, ensuring non-repudiation and replayability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If byte counting is non-deterministic due to compression or content negotiation, a request-only budget with logged response bodies is sufficient.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent can modify its own budget policy, a hardware-enforced or externally verified budget is required.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the environment can delay or drop fetch responses, a timeout-based budget must be added to prevent indefinite blocking.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent's memory is bounded and response sizes are predictable, a request-only budget with a separate memory budget may be simpler and equally auditable.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the replay system can perfectly simulate network conditions, byte counting may be unnecessary because the original responses are replayed exactly.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A dual-counter guard in the fetch loop atomically increments request count and byte count after each completed fetch. When either counter exceeds its limit, the agent transitions to a terminal state, logging an event with a unique type identifier, the policy hash, and the final counter values. The log is append-only and signed, and during replay the logged values are used instead of re-fetching to guarantee determinism.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
